text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament passed two controversial laws: on the restitution of property rights to pre-Soviet owners and a law compensating deposits lost to rampant inflation and confiscated by Soviet banks as Lithuania regained its independence. The cost of both laws may be around five billion litas.
- Three culture deputy mimisters resigned in protest at the administration style of Culture Minister Saulius Shaltenis. But Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said he would not sack the minister.
- The Bank of Lithuania decided on Thursday to extend the term for repayment of a 13.7 million litas credit to Tauras Bank to help its liquidity problems.
- Utena Beverages, the leader of the market for several years, produced less beer than Kalnapilis and Shvyturys, in May.
- Customs officials said duty revenues were 935 million litas, 335 million litas more than the same period last year.
- Unemployment in Lithuania decreased in May to 5.6 percent compared to 5.9 percent a month earlier.
- The government forecasts inflation of six percent and a budget deficit of 600 million litas in 1998.
- The government intends to impose profit tax on companies registered in soft tax zones and to reduce fines for tax evaders to 10 percent from 25 percent of annual turnover.
- Eurominister Laima Andrikiene backed the privatisation of large enterprises in the energy, transport and communication sectors during an address to parliament.
- Parliament decided to allocate two thirds of funds received from the privatisation of key enterprises to compensating lost bank savings.
- Hermis Bank is mulling an idea to distribute 8.1 million litas of a new 23 million litas share issue abroad, possibly in global depository receipts.
- A draft pension fund law is expected by June 15.
